summary: FLARE INTELLIGENCE is an interactive research and decision-support platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing “Flame in Freefall.” It makes NASA's microgravity combustion research easier to explore, compare, and understand. The platform brings together five research programmes: BASS-II, FLEX, SAFFIRE-I, SPICE, and E-FIELD Flames. It features a mission-control dashboard, experiment profiles, research search, gravity comparisons, electric-field exploration, and interactive calculations involving Grashof, Richardson, and Reynolds numbers. A dedicated fire-safety module covers material flammability, oxygen conditions, and NASA-STD-6001. Historical spacecraft fire incidents are presented separately from controlled experiments. The platform uses NASA research information and published reference material while transparently identifying unavailable raw datasets and avoiding fabricated measurements. Built using React, JavaScript, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Recharts, Node.js, and Express, it combines interactive 3D visualisation with structured research information. Its goal is to make complex combustion science accessible and help users understand how microgravity research can contribute to safer human space exploration.
details: FLARE INTELLIGENCE — Microgravity Combustion Research & Space Fire Safety Intelligence FLARE INTELLIGENCE is an interactive research and decision-support platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge's "Flame in Freefall" challenge. It addresses the difficulty of discovering, navigating, comparing and interpreting decades of NASA microgravity combustion research. The platform brings together five major research programmes: BASS-II, FLEX, SAFFIRE-I, SPICE and E-FIELD Flames. Its mission-control-inspired dashboard provides experiment profiles, scientific objectives, research highlights, published benchmark visualisations, scholarly references and dataset availability information. Users can explore the differences between normal-gravity and microgravity combustion, investigate electric-field effects on flames, search research records, compare experiments and use interactive gravity-analysis tools to examine dimensionless parameters such as Grashof, Richardson and Reynolds numbers. A dedicated fire-safety module connects combustion research with spacecraft material flammability, oxygen conditions and safety considerations. Historical spacecraft fire incidents are presented separately from controlled experiments. The project uses a React and Vite frontend, Three.js for its interactive 3D Earth visualisation, Recharts for scientific plots, and a Node.js/Express backend that serves structured research metadata and benchmark information through API endpoints. The gravity-analysis tools use scientific calculations, while the interface distinguishes published reference information from unavailable raw experimental files. Its key benefit is making complex scientific information more accessible and navigable. By connecting experimental programmes, research findings and fire-safety considerations in one interface, FLARE INTELLIGENCE aims to support students, researchers and future space-safety innovators in understanding combustion risks during long-duration human space exploration. The creative approach combines an interactive planetary visualisation, research discovery, scientific comparison and analytical tools in one unified platform. Important considerations included scientific accuracy, transparent data availability, usability, accessibility, separation of historical incidents from experiments, and avoiding fabricated measurements or unsupported conclusions. Technology: React, JavaScript, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Drei, Recharts, Node.js, Express, Python, and scikit-learn. Developed and tested on a Windows x64 laptop with an Intel Core i7 processor and 16 GB RAM. Deployed using GitHub and Render.
